issue_paraphrase: Certain low-level matching APIs of the regex ecosystem panic instead of returning a value when the caller supplies more capture slots than the pattern compiled to. The panic is a slice range error at runtime and happens even for a trivial pattern with no capture groups at all, whenever the slot buffer handed to the search is larger than the number of groups in the compiled regex. A pattern containing a group that is repeated zero times (so its captures never participate) triggers the same panic. The public API contract states the caller may provide any number of slots, so the search must instead succeed and leave the unused capture slots empty.
fix_summary: regex-automata's onepass DFA try_search_slots: clamp the number of explicit slots used for cache setup to the cache's actual explicit-slot capacity (core::cmp::min with cache.explicit_slots.len()), and when copying results back, truncate the destination slice to the length of the filled cache slots. Also adds regression tests for onepass, PikeVM and bounded backtracker.
notes: Test target is 'integration' (regex-automata/tests/lib.rs) at this commit; onepass module is gated on the default feature 'dfa' (dfa-onepass). No committed Cargo.lock; fresh resolution against crates.io works with stable rustc 1.98 (resolved memchr 2.8.3, aho-corasick 1.1.5). Incremental rebuild of regex-automata test binary ~10 s after first build; first full build a few minutes at 64 cores. Do not use Ubuntu 24.04's apt rustc 1.75 for this one: fresh dependency resolution may select crates needing a newer rustc. The task needs a recent stable toolchain.

issue_paraphrase: Searching with a pattern that contains a Unicode word boundary can return a match that is too short when the haystack contains non-ASCII characters and a literal-driven fast search path is selected. For example, a pattern that matches one or more characters, then a word boundary, then a newline, searched against a haystack like 'β77\n', is reported as matching only 3..5 instead of the full 0..5, so callers receive a truncated match whose start offset is wrong and capture spans that do not align with the true match. A full, valid match exists at the very beginning of the haystack, so the search should return that one.
fix_summary: In the meta engine's ad hoc DFA search routines (meta/limited.rs and meta/stopat.rs: dfa/hybrid half-reverse searches and end-of-input handling), always return a MatchError::quit when a quit state is entered, even if a match was tentatively found before the quit. Previously the routines returned the tentative match, which produced too-short offsets when Unicode word boundaries forced a quit. Returning the error lets the higher-level engine divert to a strategy that can handle Unicode word boundaries correctly.
notes: Test is a data-driven entry in testdata/regression.toml executed by the repo-root integration test 'suite_string::default' (test target is named 'integration' at this commit; it is renamed 'suite_string' in current HEAD). REGEX_TEST env var filters data tests (per harness output). No committed Cargo.lock; fresh crates.io resolution builds with stable rustc 1.98. Ubuntu 24.04 apt rustc (1.75) is too old if dependency resolution picks newer crates.

issue_paraphrase: A regex in which the first alternative is optional can report a match that starts too late on the haystack. For a pattern like an optional group followed by digits, then a separator, then more digits, searching '102:12:39' returns 1..9 as the match even though the true leftmost match starts at 0; some variants return an even shorter span, and the captures for the optional group come back missing or with wrong offsets. The reported match is still a real match, but it is not the leftmost one the API promises, so callers see truncated and misaligned results.
fix_summary: Adds a trip-wire in the reverse inner literal optimization (regex-automata/src/meta/limited.rs dfa_try_search_half_rev): if the DFA is not dead when the end-of-input check runs and the found match start is greater than the search start while the DFA could in principle keep searching, bail out of the optimization with a retry error so the slower, correct path produces the true leftmost match. Also records two regression cases in testdata/regression.toml.
notes: Test is a data-driven entry in testdata/regression.toml executed by the repo-root integration test 'suite_string::default' (test target named 'integration' at this commit, 'suite_string' in current HEAD). Reverse-inner strategy selection depends on the search span/haystack length; the regression entries use short haystacks that reproduce deterministically via the default regex::Regex configuration.
